newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond yields lower,gains little from data.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond yields lower,gains little from data.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were lower, largely as a reflection of continued strength in U.S. Treasuries, with slightly softer than expected local retail trade having little sustained impact.
*April U.S. non-farm payrolls report due later on Friday.
Australian bond yields were lower, largely as a reflection of continued strength in U.S. Treasuries on Thursday ahead of the key non-farm payrolls later on Friday.

Domestic retail trade data for March and the first quarter were slightly softer than median expectations, but any thoughts of an imminent easing in monetary policy have already been dashed following Thursday's strong wages data.

Yields edge down slightly in immediate response to the retail data, but the market failed to sustain the move with sentiment severely dented by the wages outcome and the steep sell-off that followed them.
Retail trade fell 0.3 percent after an expected flat result, and quarterly rose 2.2 percent versus an expected 2.4 percent.

The focus switches to the U.S. and the release of the April jobs report and analysts will be scanning the data for any facts that can sustain this week's rally, which has partly reflected hopes of a balanced U.S. budget accord.

"What you see today may not necessarily be the flavour tomorrow and it's going to be the similar volatility over the few next weeks. We won't get the the longer-term direction until we get the employment data under our belts both in the U.S. and here," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.

The local market retraced some ground against the U.S. after blowing out sharply on Thursday, but the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread is still well above the sub-100 basis points seen at the tail-end of last week. The local yield curve continued its post-wages data flattening trend.
